answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by locking tokens in a public bond that is slashed when a challenge proves their identities are controlled by one operator. A challenger posts a smaller bond and must supply evidence before a fixed deadline; false claims lose their stake. Splitting capital across fake accounts gives no extra weight, while each account raises the cost of monitoring and defending its bond. The delta between honest returns and the risk of forfeiture makes a ledge costly to occupy, even beside a busy wharf.
